consistency and voice: repeated phrases, tonal drift, name collisions, redundant sections, flavor-vs-rules balance

payload.statement:
# HOL Council — ch02 Character Creation

Chapter under review: ch02 (quarto-book/chapters/02-character-creation.qmd), "Creating Your Hero", 579 lines. The book's character-creation chapter: two-phase creation (Level 0 Background then Level 1 Class), Steps 1-11, quick-build sidebar, the worked example of Makeva Quickfoot (lines 228-266), and eight build templates (Mage: Arcanist/Intellect, Priest: Shepherd/Leader, Thief: Blade/Shadow, Fighter: Protector/Unbalanced, lines 270-579). These templates are the canonical stat anchors for the party and the primary DP-math worked examples in the book; ch08's discipline examples reference them ("Sera the Arcanist... 1 Fire and 1 Energy at creation", ch08:204-210).

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan. Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files ONE finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope
Findings cite [02-character-creation.qmd:line]. Mechanics findings state the broken value and the expected value.

Cross-chapter canon anchors (use the AUTHORITATIVE chapters as reference, not this chapter):
- class starting bundles + signature texts = ch05 (05-classes.qmd) — the class chapters' authoritative phrasing. E.g. the Blade's signature (ch05:88) is "Swift Blade: use Agility instead of Brawn when attacking with blades. Gain the Precise Stab ability, bonus damage when exploiting an opening"; the Protector's "Bastion: Spend your movement to enter a defensive stance. Add +1 to your Protection Value for the round" (ch05:49); the Unbalanced's "Edge of Chaos: On a Strong hit, deal +1 damage tier (one row up on the damage budget) but roll on the d6 Backlash Table" (ch05:336) — this was locked in PR #331, killing the old "+4 bonus damage" flat rider.
- discipline taxonomy = ch08 (08-disciplines.qmd): 23 Disciplines in 9 categories. "Starting disciplines from ancestry, culture, and class are always rank 1 in distinct disciplines. You may not spend both picks on the same discipline to start with rank 2" (ch08:83).
- class cost tables = ch05 class sections (Protector ch05:60-71, Blade ch05:96-107, Arcanist ch05:140-151, Shepherd ch05:171-190, Intellect ch05:210-228, Odd ch05:258-272, Leader ch05:305-317, Unbalanced ch05:349-368, Shadow ch05:400-412). Home 1/2/4, Adjacent 2/4/8, Foreign 3/6/12, Opposed 4/8/16.
- class favored-skill lists = ch05 (Protector ch05:51, Blade ch05:90, Arcanist ch05:135, Shepherd ch05:174, Intellect ch05:213, Odd ch05:252, Leader ch05:293, Unbalanced ch05:349, Shadow ch05:396).
- class starting kits = ch05 class sections (e.g. Protector ch05:54, Blade ch05:92, Shadow ch05:398).
- movement canon = ch03:68: "30 feet per round for most heroes. Dwarves and halflings move 25 feet, heavy armor slows you by 5 feet".
- HP canon = ch02 Table 2.3 itself (10 + Fortitude + Knowledge at L1); Dwarf Sturdy +2 max HP (ch04:63/66).
- skills roster = ch07:108-156 (Survival is Fortitude, Endurance is Fortitude, Perception is Reason, Craft is Reason, etc.). The 22-skill roster (ch07 header).
- signature flavor: Ch05 signatures carry unlocked ability names (e.g. Swift Blade unlocks Precise Stab as a named ability).
- decisions-pending context: #16 (2026-08-15, implemented) changed Priest kits to leather armor (DR 2) — verify templates reflect leather, not chain shirt; #17 (implemented) added the movement row 30 ft with dwarf/halfling 25 ft and heavy-armor -5 ft notes — Table 2.3's Movement row should already carry it; #18 (implemented) rank-2 deepening at creation is allowed ("2 same" shape, rank costs per class table); #22 (resolved) Edge of Chaos is "+1 damage tier", never "+4 bonus damage"; ch02 Wave-1 (PR #306, 2026-08-15) fixed stale ancestry lines, Turn Undead->Turn Unholy, spell names Mending Touch/Sanctuary, Intellect any-pick, Gorma Blades->Protection rank 1, movement row, focus pouch renames, Arcane Shield "+1 Protection Value", and misapplied "favored" tags x3.

Book conventions every lens applies: zero em-dashes (restructure sentences, never find-replace); flat damage budgets Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21; card costs flat 2/4/8 DP; one-roll principle; no stale retired vocabulary (DA not GM, class names from the 9-class roster, spell/ability names must exist in the spell chapters or ch05/ch09 tables); placeholder art is acceptable in a draft.

Specific areas worth checking (findings are yours to file or dismiss):
- Every template's derived stats: HP = 10 + Fort + Know (+2 if Dwarf), Initiative = Agility mod, Movement = 30 ft (25 dwarf/halfling, -5 heavy armor), Carry = 10 + Brawn x 5. Check Makeva (Halfling, line 262: "Movement 30 ft"), Haldra (Dwarf Hill, line 385), Gorma (Dwarf Mountain heavy armor, line 538 "Movement 20 ft"), Pip (Halfling, line 499), and all nine templates against the formulas and the character's own attributes/armor.
- Every template's class signature wording vs ch05's signature line: Sera Arcanist (line 294), Lirael Intellect (line 333), Haldra Shepherd (line 372), Marta Leader (line 410), Vaelith Blade (line 448), Pip Shadow (line 486), Gorma Protector (line 525), Corwin Unbalanced (line 564). Watch specifically for the Edge of Chaos phrasing in Corwin's template (line 564) — "+4 bonus damage" is the dead flat rider; ch05:336 says "+1 damage tier".
- Class Discipline claims in each template vs ch05/ch08 class bundles (line 249 Odd "Blades and Water", line 294 Arcanist "1 Fire, 1 Energy", line 333 Intellect "1 Lore, 1 any (takes Tactics)", line 372 Shepherd "Protection + Animal", line 410 Leader "Tactics + Protection", line 448 Blade "Blades + Stealth", line 486 Shadow "Stealth + Sleight", line 525 Protector "any Weapon + Armor", line 564 Unbalanced "Fire + Water"). An Unbalanced human who picks Fire for the human ancestry AND gets Fire from the class would start with 2 Fire from two free picks — against ch08:83's "rank 1 in distinct disciplines... not both picks on the same discipline"? Check each template's ancestry/culture/class overlap against ch08:83.
- Cost/DP arithmetic in each template: background DP = 8 + Knowledge + Fortitude, class DP = 8, Human Versatile = +1 DP at Level 0. Verify the totals column ("Total: X DP. All spent.") matches the sum of purchases and the DP pool in every template and in Makeva's worked example. Watch "favored" tags: only skills on the class's ch05 favored list may be tagged favored (Arcanist: Alchemy/Arcana/History/Lore/Nature; Leader: Persuasion/Perception/Insight/Survival/Endurance; check each).
- Discipline-rank purchases in background DP vs the class's cost table: Marta Leader "Blades Discipline, rank 2 (2 DP)" (line 403), Vaelith Blade "Sleight Discipline, rank 1 (1 DP)" (line 444), Gorma Protector "Protection Discipline, rank 1 (1 DP)" (line 521), Haldra Shepherd "Life Discipline, rank 1 (1 DP)" (line 368). Verify against ch05 cost tables and #18 rank-2 rules.
- Ability names bought in class DP must exist as real cards (ch05 tables or spell chapters). Verify Ember Lance/Burning Volley (Arcanist), Mending Touch/Sanctuary (Shepherd), Exploit Chaos/Improvised Solution (Odd), Interpose/Parry (Protector), Sap/Perception/Acrobatics (Shadow), Precise Stab's existence (Blade signature references it — does a Precise Stab card exist anywhere in ch05/ch09/ch11/ch12?), Rallying Cry/Tactical Insight/Force Dart, etc.
- Kit line vs the class's ch05 starting kit: Sera (line 305), Lirael (line 344), Haldra (line 383), Marta (line 421), Vaelith (line 459), Pip (line 497), Gorma (line 536), Corwin (line 575), Makeva (line 260). Watch leather armor for the two Priests, focus pouch/spellbook/holy symbol matches, and any "component pouch" leftovers (renamed to focus pouch in #309).
- Culture discipline grants: each culture line in the templates should record the culture's granted Disciplines (per the Step 4 culture table in this chapter) or the free discipline for adaptable cultures; e.g. Sera Imperial "Free Discipline: Energy" (line 282), Lirael High Elf "Energy + Blades" (line 321). Check whether each template records its culture disciplines, and whether the culture grant duplicates an ancestry/class grant against ch08:83.
- Makeva worked example: DP math (lines 240-258), class line "Gains 2 Disciplines from different categories (Blades and Water)" (line 249) — Makeva is a Halfling whose ancestry grants Blades; does the Odd class grant stack or duplicate? Does the example's Step 4 culture line record Riverfolk's disciplines? Check consistency with ch08:83 and ch05's Odd.
- Ancestry/culture trait references: Lucky (Halfling), Sturdy (Dwarf), Elven Grace, Versatile — and any "boon" usage (a boon = extra d6, ch06; "add one boon" is the ch04 trait phrasing).
- Cross-chapter contamination: class-name references, spell/ability names, armor DR values (chain mail DR 5 per ch16:39; leather DR 2 per ch16:34; robes DR 0 if referenced — verify a "robes" armor entry exists or note it), and skill names vs ch07.
- The chapter's own rules text vs its templates: does Step 5's "What You Can Buy" table allow everything the templates buy (rank-2 deepening is addressed in Step 5 prose line 136; verify the table or prose covers Discipline first rank AND rank-2 deepening)? Do the quick-build and two-phase callouts match the worked examples?
- Layout/presentation: heading hierarchy (## vs ###), table formatting, the pagebreak usage, callout structure, any render issues you can verify by grepping the .qmd (e.g., the anchor label block at lines 3-5 duplicates the heading anchor — that is the book-wide pattern, verify before flagging).

Disposition tiers (the librarian synthesizes these in the recommendation):
  TIER 1 mechanical — chapter-local, zero mechanics change, no content judgment (heading/label, wording, em-dashes, table rows, stale refs, page flow).
  TIER 2 substantive — rewrites or multi-sentence fixes that change content but not rules (a line rephrased to match canon, a paragraph restructured).
  TIER 3 design decisions — anything that touches rules, canon identities, or book-wide convention; route to decisions-pending for Bruce, with a recommended default.

payload.argument: The chapter is not publishable as a unit: this audit confirms a wrong stat value in the Makeva worked example (halfling movement printed at 30 ft against the chapter's own Table 2.3 and ch03 canon), a Human template whose background pool ignores the Versatile bonus its own ancestry line grants while the two sibling Human templates apply it, a worked example whose culture step drops Riverfolk's granted disciplines, and a template reprinting a retired signature phrasing. Disposition tiers: the stat-value fixes and the pagebreak-marker pattern are TIER 1 mechanical (chapter-local, no rules or content change; the page-flow risk needs a render check); reconciling Sera's pool, recording Makeva's culture disciplines, and rephrasing Corwin's signature to match ch05:336 are TIER 2 substantive (content rewritten, zero rules change); the recurring duplication of free-grant disciplines (Sera and Corwin each double Fire, Makeva would hold Blades three times) collides with ch08:83's distinctness sentence and ch02 nowhere says how fixed-grant overlaps resolve, which is a TIER 3 design decision routed to Bruce with a default that starting grants stay distinct. Verified issues are enumerated below; none is a judgment about which character should buy what, only what must change for the chapter to agree with itself and with canon.

evidence.claim: Makeva is a Halfling, yet the worked example at [02-character-creation.qmd:262] prints Movement 30 ft, where the chapter's own Table 2.3 would cap a halfling at 25 ft; the sibling Pip template at [02-character-creation.qmd:499] shows the correct 25 ft (halfling) form. Tier 1: single stat value, chapter-local, zero rules change.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Movement 30 ft

evidence.claim: The Movement row of Table 2.3 at [02-character-creation.qmd:193] sets dwarves and halflings at 25 ft, so the 30 ft printed at line 262 is the chapter contradicting its own derived-stat table.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 30 ft (Dwarves and halflings: 25 ft

evidence.claim: Movement canon outside the chapter (03-attributes.qmd:68) agrees with Table 2.3 that halflings move 25 feet; every other stat block in the section follows it (Haldra at 385, Pip at 499, Gorma at 538 with heavy armor), isolating line 262 as the anomaly.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Dwarves and halflings move 25 feet

evidence.claim: Sera's template records the Human Versatile trait granting +1 DP at Level 0 ([02-character-creation.qmd:280]) yet its Background DP line at [02-character-creation.qmd:284] totals 10 DP without adding it, while Marta at line 401 and Corwin at line 554 both fold the bonus into their stated pools. The bare arithmetic slip is Tier 1; deciding how the missing DP is spent is a content choice, so the net disposition is Tier 2.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Versatile:** +1 DP at Level 0

evidence.claim: With Versatile applied, Sera should hold 11 background DP and spend all of it; her template states 10 and spends 10, so either the trait is silently unhonored or the spend is short by one point, and the template must be reconciled either way.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 8 + Know 2 + Fort 0 = 10 DP

evidence.claim: Makeva's Step 4 at [02-character-creation.qmd:238] records only the Acrobatics skill bonus and never the Riverfolk discipline grant, unlike every build template, which records its culture grant (e.g. lines 282, 321, 513, 552); Tier 2 content gap with zero rules change.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Step 4, Culture:** Riverfolk. +1 bonus to Acrobatics

evidence.claim: The chapter's own culture table at [02-character-creation.qmd:89] grants Riverfolk Blades + Archery, so a reader following Makeva through Step 4 cannot account for her full discipline load at Step 6.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Riverfolk | Acrobatics or Sleight of Hand | Blades + Archery

evidence.claim: Corwin's Unbalanced template at [02-character-creation.qmd:564] reprints Edge of Chaos with a flat +4 damage rider that the class canon retired; rephrasing the one line to match ch05:336 is Tier 2 substantive (canon-matching rewrite, zero rules change).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: on Strong hit, +4 bonus damage but roll d6 backlash

evidence.claim: The authoritative signature at 05-classes.qmd:336 (locked in PR #331) defines Edge of Chaos as one damage tier up on the damage budget on a Strong hit plus the d6 Backlash roll, with no flat-damage rider.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: deal +1 damage tier (one row up on the damage budget)

evidence.claim: The eight-template layout pattern is verifiable in source: the two templates inside each archetype pair are separated only by a bare rule (lines 311, 389, 465, 542) and the pagebreak appears only after each pair's second template (lines 350, 427, 503), so the second head of each pair (313, 391, 467, 544) opens mid-page after a bare rule; whether a head actually strands at a page foot is a rendered-layout fact the .qmd cannot prove and needs a check in the built PDF. Tier 1 layout, chapter-local.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: {{< pagebreak >}}

evidence.claim: Sera's free grants overlap: the Human any-one pick is Fire at [02-character-creation.qmd:280], the Arcanist class bundle at line 294 adds 1 Fire and 1 Energy, and her Imperial free pick at line 282 adds Energy, so Fire and Energy each arrive twice from free starting sources, against the distinctness sentence of ch08:83.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Any one Discipline (takes Fire)

evidence.claim: The class line at [02-character-creation.qmd:294] grants 1 Fire and 1 Energy, duplicating Sera's ancestry pick of Fire.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Gains 1 Fire, 1 Energy

evidence.claim: Discipline canon (08-disciplines.qmd:83) requires the free grants arriving from lineage, upbringing, and class each to sit at first rank in a separate discipline, and it bars spending two picks on one discipline merely to begin at second rank; ch02 contains no text resolving a fixed grant that duplicates an earlier one (a Halfling Riverfolk, for instance, would receive Blades twice from Steps 3-4 alone).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: always rank 1 in distinct disciplines

evidence.claim: The discipline chapter's worked example that references this template's Sera counts exactly one Fire at creation (ch08:204-206), which the doubled Fire grant in the ch02 template cannot produce under ch08:83.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Her class gives her 1 Fire and 1 Energy at creation

evidence.claim: Corwin doubles Fire the same way: Human pick Fire at [02-character-creation.qmd:550] and the Unbalanced bundle 1 Fire + 1 Water at line 564.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Gains 1 Fire, 1 Water

evidence.claim: Makeva's Blades recurs across three free sources: Halfling ancestry (line 236), the Riverfolk culture grant (table line 89, unrecorded in her Step 4), and the Odd pick of Blades and Water at line 249; ch08:83's distinctness rule leaves no legal reading unless a grant changes or a duplicate rule is written, which is the Tier 3 question.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Gains 2 Disciplines from different categories (Blades and Water)

evidence.claim: The chapter's own discipline-source prose at lines 128-142 enumerates how grants arrive (ancestry, culture, DP, class) but never says what happens when two sources grant the same discipline; writing that rule touches rules text, so it is a Tier 3 design decision for Bruce with a recommended default that starting grants stay distinct and fixed-grant duplicates get explicit resolution text.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Every Discipline your hero possesses comes from a specific source

payload.argument: Free-discipline grants collide inside the chapter's own builds, and no rule resolves the collision. Steps 3-6 tell the player each source 'grants' a Discipline, but never what happens when a grant lands on one you already hold; ch04 has no such rule either. Sera's template therefore grants Fire twice (Human any-one pick plus Arcanist class) and Energy twice (Imperial free Discipline plus Arcanist class); Corwin's template grants Fire twice; Makeva's worked example grants Blades three times once the Riverfolk culture table is honored, though her Step 4 write-up silently drops those grants. Canon ch08:83 requires all free starting Disciplines to be rank 1 in distinct disciplines, with only paid Background-DP deepening allowed to reach rank 2. Because ch02 never states the duplicate outcome, the chapter supports two readings, both broken: a player copying Sera can claim free rank-2 Fire at level 1 (skipping the 2-DP deepening that Marta pays and the level-3 pick ch08:208 says an Arcanist must spend for a second Fire, and clearing the longsword's 2-Blades entry for free); or the earlier grant is silently voided, wasting the ancestry/culture pick with no reroute option and falsifying ch02's own claim that a starting hero typically holds 4-6 Disciplines before spending DP. Also tested and found sound: rank-2 deepening via Background DP is legal under ch08:83, Adept/Master card purchases remain blocked at level 1, and the quick-build attribute spread fits the caps. Two further breaks surfaced in the same templates: Corwin's Edge of Chaos still prints the retired flat +4 rider instead of the canon one-tier bump, and Makeva's halfling moves 30 ft where her own chapter's table says 25 ft.

evidence.claim: Sera's template grants Fire through both the Human any-one ancestry pick and the Arcanist class, and Energy through both the Imperial free Discipline and the Arcanist class, giving two no-cost grants of each.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Gains 1 Fire, 1 Energy

evidence.claim: Makeva's worked example grants Blades from Halfling ancestry and again as an Odd class pick, while the Step 4 table lists Riverfolk as granting Blades and Archery, which her Step 4 write-up never records.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Gains 2 Disciplines from different categories (Blades and Water)

evidence.claim: Canon requires every free starting Discipline from ancestry, culture, or class to be rank 1 in a distinct Discipline; two picks may not start a rank-2, and only Background-DP deepening may raise a creation Discipline to rank 2.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: always rank 1 in distinct disciplines

evidence.claim: The disciplines chapter's own Sera example assumes she starts with exactly one Fire and must spend her level-3 pick to gain the second, which only holds if her ch02 ancestry Fire grant counts for nothing.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Her class gives her 1 Fire and 1 Energy

evidence.claim: Weapon entry requirements make the duplicate-grant hole spendable: a longsword demands 2 Blades, so free duplicate grants bypass the paid deepening other builds need for the same access.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: A Longsword needs *2 Blades*

evidence.claim: Corwin's template still prints the retired Edge of Chaos rider as a flat +4 damage bonus on Strong hits.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +4 bonus damage but roll d6 backlash

evidence.claim: Canon, locked via PR #331, defines Edge of Chaos as stepping one row up the damage budget on a Strong hit rather than adding a flat +4.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +1 damage tier (one row up on the damage budget)

payload.argument: The flagship Unbalanced build template (Corwin) restates the class's Edge of Chaos signature as a flat +4 bonus damage rider on Strong hits, but the authoritative class chapter defines that signature as shifting the damage result up one tier on the damage budget, and no other text in the book supports a flat +4 rider. The recorded design history resolved Edge of Chaos to the tier-shift form, so this template line preserves a retired mechanic and must be reworded to the +1 damage tier value; the fix is confined to the signature clause at line 564, leaving the rest of the template intact.

evidence.claim: Corwin's build template in this chapter says Edge of Chaos adds a flat +4 bonus damage whenever he rolls a Strong hit, balanced by a d6 backlash roll.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: on Strong hit, +4 bonus damage but roll d6 backlash

evidence.claim: The class chapter's own signature text for Edge of Chaos instead grants one extra damage tier, meaning the next row up on the damage budget, on a Strong hit.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: deal +1 damage tier (one row up on the damage budget)

payload.argument: Corwin's Unbalanced template reprints Edge of Chaos with the retired flat rider, telling readers that a Strong hit adds a fixed 4 bonus damage. Canon now expresses the signature as raising the result one row on the shared damage budget, and the weapons rework removed flat bonus-damage riders from the whole book, so a hero built from this template learns a mechanical effect the class no longer possesses. The quoted wording must be corrected to the tier-bump phrasing used in the class chapter.

evidence.claim: Corwin's class line still grants Edge of Chaos as a flat 4 bonus damage on a Strong hit, the pre-rework wording, where the expected effect is a one-step rise on the shared damage-budget table.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: on Strong hit, +4 bonus damage but roll d6 backlash

evidence.claim: The authoritative Unbalanced signature, locked in by the weapons rework and the resolved Edge of Chaos decision, states the effect as moving up one damage tier on the budget with the same d6 backlash roll, and contains no fixed number.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: deal +1 damage tier (one row up on the damage budget)

evidence.claim: The damage-budget rule declares flat numbers the law for all damage expressions, and the rework deleted flat bonus-damage riders such as this one from card text book-wide.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The numbers are flat damage points.

payload.argument: Table 2.2's Vibe column is the book's one-line snapshot of each class, quoting the class taglines from 05-classes.qmd, but two of the nine rows carry shortened forms of lines the class chapter prints in full, so the book now holds two different versions of two canonical class identities; the excised fragments are exactly the clauses carrying each class's signature flavor (the one-strike finish, the willingness to pay chaos's price). The Unbalanced row's drift repeats in its own build template, where the Edge of Chaos signature copy no longer matches the classes chapter and the formal table name is lowercased, so all class-voice restatements in this chapter need one alignment pass against the 05-classes.qmd epigraphs and signature lines. Minimal fix: restore the full taglines in the Blade and Unbalanced rows and align the line-564 signature copy; wording-level, no design change.

evidence.claim: The class-roster table quotes the Blade tagline without its final beat, producing a truncated version of the canonical line.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Strike once. Strike true.

evidence.claim: The Blade class section opens with the complete three-beat version of the same tagline, which the roster row appears to abbreviate without marking the abridgement.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Strike once. Strike true. Strike last.

evidence.claim: The roster row for the Unbalanced class stops its tagline after the first sentence.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Power has a price.

evidence.claim: The Unbalanced class section completes that tagline with a second clause carrying the class's self-destructive bargain, which the truncated roster version loses.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Power has a price. I'm willing to pay.

evidence.claim: The Unbalanced build template restates the Edge of Chaos signature in copy that diverges from the classes chapter and refers to the mechanic generically instead of by its formal table name.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +4 bonus damage but roll d6 backlash

evidence.claim: The classes chapter's authoritative phrasing frames the same signature as a damage-tier increase plus a roll on the named d6 Backlash Table.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: On a Strong hit, deal +1 damage tier

payload.argument: The chapter's only full step-by-step walkthrough of the 11-step procedure, the Makeva Quickfoot worked example (lines 228-266), is not a faithful model of its own rules. Its Step 4 records only Riverfolk's skill bonus and never the culture's two granted Disciplines, even though the chapter's Step 4 table (line 89) and Step 4 prose (line 72) make those grants mandatory and every one of the eight templates that follow records them. Because the grants go unrecorded, Step 6's Odd acquisitions ('Blades and Water', line 249) collide with disciplines Makeva already holds from her halfling ancestry (line 236) and from Riverfolk, so the example's final character cannot be reproduced under the chapter's own rules: a reader copying it silently loses two granted Disciplines, and Step 9's reported movement rate (line 262) contradicts the chapter's own Derived Statistics table, which fixes halflings at 25 ft (line 193) and which the sibling Pip template applies correctly (line 499). Smallest fix: in the example's Step 4, record Riverfolk's Discipline grant and reconcile the Step 6 Odd grants (e.g., grant only Water, or choose a non-overlapping culture such as Wanderer), and correct Step 9 to 25 ft. This is broken, not merely incomplete: the flagship teaching device states a wrong rule output and omits a mandatory step that every other example in the chapter performs.

evidence.claim: In the Makeva walkthrough, the Culture step lists only the Acrobatics skill bonus — no mention of the two Disciplines Riverfolk grants per the chapter's own Step 4 table.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Riverfolk. +1 bonus to Acrobatics

evidence.claim: The Step 4 culture table in the same chapter states that Riverfolk grants the Blades and Archery Disciplines — the very output the example omits.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Riverfolk | Acrobatics or Sleight of Hand | Blades + Archery

evidence.claim: The Odd class grants in Makeva's Step 6 name Blades as a fresh acquisition even though ancestry (Step 3) already granted it and Riverfolk (Step 4) would grant it again, so the example's discipline ledger cannot be reconciled with the chapter's rules.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Gains 2 Disciplines from different categories (Blades and Water)

evidence.claim: By contrast, each of the eight build templates that follow records its culture's Discipline grants, e.g. the Leader template names both Polearms and Protection — showing the worked example is the outlier.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Disciplines: Polearms + Protection.

evidence.claim: The example's Step 9 states a 30 ft movement rate for a halfling, contradicting the chapter's own Derived Statistics table, which sets halflings at 25 ft (the halfling Pip template at line 499 gets this right).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Movement 30 ft.

evidence.claim: Table 2.3, the rule the example should follow, explicitly caps halflings at 25 ft of movement.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Dwarves and halflings: 25 ft

payload.argument: Build-verified page-flow defect in the template gallery (the chapter's reference-sheet centerpiece). Forced page breaks fall only between archetype pairs (lines 350/427/503) while each pair's two members are joined by a plain thematic-break rule (lines 311/389/465/542), encoding a two-templates-per-page assumption. In the rendered PDF each template runs roughly a full page, so on pages 45/47/49/51 the divider ornament and the second template's heading are stranded at the page foot while the template body spills onto the next page: all four second templates (Intellect, Leader, Shadow, Unbalanced) straddle the break, and Mage: Intellect's heading is orphaned with no body line beneath it. Fix: force a page break before each of the eight templates and drop the four intra-pair rules, matching the per-section pagebreak rhythm used in ch05; the chapter then closes cleanly at line 579 with no trailing break. Em-dash law, heading levels, and template block coverage otherwise pass.

evidence.claim: Each archetype pair is internally joined by a bare thematic-break rule and a forced page break appears only after the pair's second template, so the layout presumes two full templates share a page.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: {{< pagebreak >}}

evidence.claim: The Arcanist template fills page 45; under its closing Name line the divider ornament and the Mage: Intellect heading sit alone at the page foot, with Intellect's entire stat block starting on page 46.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: ❧ Mage: Intellect
evidence.source: build output: quarto-book/_output/Heroes-of-Legend.pdf page 45 (built 2026-09-04 from this source)

payload.rationale: Round 1 closed 7-0 against the chapter; every refute is un-rebutted and all seven converge on a small, verifiable defect set. (1) The retired Edge of Chaos rider is the strongest consensus item: researcher (f-003), game-architect (f-004), contrarian (f-002), librarian (f-001) and author (f-005) all cite the same two lines — [02-character-creation.qmd:564] prints '+4 bonus damage' while canon 05-classes.qmd:336 (PR #331, weapons rework) defines the signature as '+1 damage tier (one row up on the damage budget)'; the flat-rider phrasing is dead book-wide under the zero-rider law and ch08:187's flat-numbers rule. (2) Makeva's halfling Movement 30 ft (line 262) contradicts Table 2.3 line 193, ch03:68, and the sibling Pip template (line 499, 25 ft) — flagged independently by librarian, contrarian, and editor-in-chief. (3) The Makeva walkthrough omits Riverfolk's two granted Disciplines (editor-in-chief f-006; table line 89 vs Step 4 write-up line 238), making the flagship teaching device irreproducible. (4) Sera's missing Versatile +1 DP (librarian f-001) is an internal-template inconsistency against the two sibling Human templates (Marta line 401, Corwin line 554). (5) The author lens (f-005) caught two truncated class taglines in Table 2.2's Vibe column (Blade line 163, Unbalanced line 169) vs the full epigraphs at ch05:82/:330. (6) The layout-expert (f-007) build-verified (against quarto-book/_output/Heroes-of-Legend.pdf pages 45/47/49/51) that the archetype-pair pagebreak pattern strands the second template's heading at the page foot; fix is chapter-local pagebreak placement. (7) The contrarian (f-002) and librarian (f-001) both elevate the free-grant duplication hole (Sera Fire x2 + Energy x2; Corwin Fire x2; Makeva Blades x3) as the one genuine rules question: ch08:83 requires free starting grants to be rank 1 in distinct disciplines, ch02 never says what happens when fixed grants overlap, and ch08:204-208's own Sera example presumes exactly one Fire at creation. Items (1)-(6) are mechanical or substantive with canon-determined fixes; item (7) is the only design-decision that routes to Bruce, with a recommended default (distinct starting grants) anchored on ch08:83. Layout lens separately confirms em-dash law (zero), heading hierarchy, and template block coverage all pass. No sealed rulings exist; rulings_applied is empty; dissent is empty (7-0 reject, no support position to record).
